messages:
incident-bot: URGENT: dedicated pool dp-acme-01 reporting GPU saturation (tenant=AcmeCorp). All nodes >96% for 9m. Pager triggered to #incidents and @oncall.

alex: oncall here. what failure mode are we seeing?

maya: p95 token latency spiked from ~180ms -> ~1.6s across their routes; queue depth increasing. A handful of inference requests hit the 60s timeout and returned 504. No node OOMs.

tom: checking autoscaler and pool config. dp-acme-01 settings: `committed_gpus=22`, `autoscale.max=22`, `burst_policy=disabled`, `isolation_level=strict`. Autoscaler logs: "scale blocked - burst disallowed and committed limit reached".

sophia: Acme contract explicitly required no bursting into shared pools because of compliance audit last quarter. They accepted higher committed capacity instead.

ryan: customer ops flagged production impact to some end-users; CSM asked for immediate mitigation.

nikita: possible mitigations: (A) temporarily enable burst to borrow shared nodes; (B) emergency manual quota add (provision extra dedicated nodes); (C) route non-critical traffic away; (D) degrade model size for some routes to reduce GPU usage.

alex: prioritize fastest low-risk approach. Thoughts?

tom: fastest low-risk is manual quota grant: `rictl quota add dp-acme-01 --gpus 3` — gives dedicated nodes without touching burst policy. Takes ~2m to allocate. Enabling burst is instant but relaxes the isolation contract temporarily.

maya: if we go manual quota, expect cache cold-starts but better than cross-tenant burst. Throttling non-essential routes buys time immediately.

sophia: I'll reach out to Acme account lead and legal to notify them of any emergency changes. We should avoid unilateral contract changes unless critical.

alex: plan: 1) throttle low-priority routes for Acme immediately 2) apply manual quota + monitor 3) if manual quota insufficient, ask Acme for emergency temporary burst approval.

nikita: executing throttles now: `routes.acme.*.(logs|analytics|batch) -> rate_limit 20%`
deploy-bot: Throttle applied: routes matched, ruleset=r-3201, actor=nikita, status=applied

tom: issuing quota add now: 
```bash
rictl quota add dp-acme-01 --gpus 3 --reason "emergency: tenant gpu exhaustion"
```
deploy-bot: Change submitted CHG-13011 by tom; auto-approve path used. Allocation in progress.

maya: allocator shows 2 of 3 nodes provisioned, queue depth falling. p95 improving to ~700ms within 4m. No new 60s timeouts after throttles+quota.

ryan: informed Acme via secure channel: "We've applied temporary throttles and added emergency capacity; performance should stabilize. We'll follow up with a capacity plan." They responded asking about data isolation and whether any workloads touched shared hardware.

sophia: responded: "No data plane changes; manual quota adds dedicated nodes to your pool only. We'll only seek burst if absolutely necessary and with your approval."

alex: good. next steps: - keep throttles until p95 < 400ms for 20m - run a tailored load replay from Acme sample prompts to size committed gpus - prepare proposal: committed_gpus 22 -> 30 and optionally `burst_cap=4` (opt-in) - assign postmortem owner

maya: I'll run the load replay in the staging mirror with their prompt set and synthetic arrival pattern in 6h and share GPU sustained usage curves. Archiving traces to s3://redwood-incidents/dp-acme-01/2100001234/trace.tar.gz

tom: I'll draft cost delta for +8 gpus and for enabling controlled burst cap=4. Also include rollback plan and deployment schedule.

sophia: legal approved a one-time emergency manual quota for 48h under continuity clause. I'll coordinate billing for potential credits; CSM looped in.

ikita: removing throttles gradually as queue normalizes. Doing step-down to 50% -> 100% over 10m window.
deploy-bot: Throttle update applied by nikita: 20% -> 50%

maya: metrics 12m post-mitigation: p95 steady ~330-360ms, queue depth nominal, no new 504s.

alex: excellent. create tickets: CHG-13011 (quota add), TKT-30301 (capacity uplift proposal), PM-802 (postmortem, owner=maya). Keep monitoring for 72h with oncall notifications.

deploy-bot: Tickets CHG-13011, TKT-30301, PM-802 created and linked to incident. Monitoring subscription updated: dp-acme-01 gpu>90% -> notify @oncall + #incidents for 72h.

ryan: customer update posted: concise note and timeline. They asked for a runbook entry for future spikes; we'll schedule a joint review next week.

sophia: planning a contract amendment if they want persistent burst opt-in. I'll schedule a call with the account team. :calendar:

alex: closing pager for now. Leave thread open for postmortem and scheduling. Reopen if metrics regress. Postmortem owner: maya.

incident-bot: Incident resolved: mitigation applied and verified. Logging incident code INC-2100001234."
